subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw expose diagnostics-only declared/effective tool visibility first, or also add a default-off strict inheritance mode that fails sessions when declared and effective tools diverge?
rationale: The choice defines whether agent tool config remains a declaration below lower security layers or becomes an enforcement contract that can fail or conflict with sandbox, subagent, runtime-host, provider, and ACP restrictions.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Expose declared, effective, removed, and blocked tools with structured layer reasons while preserving current lower-layer clipping behavior.

options.title: Default-Off Strict Parity
options.body: Add a strict option that fails closed on divergence and include docs, protocol fields, and fresh-install plus upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Current Model
options.body: Keep runtime clipping authoritative and document that agent tool config is not the final session tool contract.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, removed, and blocked tools with structured layer reasons while preserving current lower-layer clipping behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent capability-profile and one-profile policy refactor history makes this the closest current owner signal for the cross-cutting agent policy and security-boundary decision.
